subject: Request: Model route immutability for ClinTrial pilot (EU-bound)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dr. Emily Zhao <e.zhao@clintrial.ai>, Paul Rivera <paul@clintrial.ai>
Date: Sat, 4 Nov 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Request: Model route immutability for ClinTrial pilot (EU-bound)

Team —

ClinTrial AI is finalizing the pilot SOW and they have a strict regulatory requirement: all inference for the pilot must execute inside the EU and must be bound to a single vetted model variant for the duration of the pilot. They explicitly asked for an immutable routing commitment (no automatic fallback to other regions/variants).

Key asks (from the customer):
- Route all traffic for the pilot to an EU-only variant: "redwood-clinical-v1-quant" (they need deterministic output).
- No automatic fallback to non-EU variants or hosted shared pool.
- Data residency: logs/inputs/outputs must remain in EU and be retained only 30 days for the pilot.
- KMS-backed encryption and audit logs enabled for keys.

Timeline: pilot starts 2028-11-20; we need a sign-off on feasibility by EOD 2028-11-06 so ClinTrial can sign the SOW.

I've attached the draft SOW and their SOC2 summary.

Questions for engineering/ops: can we provide an operational carveout that guarantees the route immutability and also preserves our autoscaling/availability responsibilities? If not, what are the minimal alternative safeguards we can promise (e.g., reserved capacity, manual failover only with approvals)?

Markus / Legal: any contractual or indemnity flags if we commit to a hard routing lock for the pilot?

Laura / Security: what additional controls do you need before approving an EU-only route?

I'll consolidate and reply to Dr. Zhao once we have an internal view.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 415 555 0148

Subject: Re: Request: Model route immutability for ClinTrial pilot (EU-bound)

Marissa — thanks for the heads up and attachments. A few follow-ups so I can scope the work and ops risk: 

1) Traffic profile: expected QPS and peak concurrency for pilot (estimates are fine). We need this to size reserved capacity or suggest a Dedicated pool.
2) SLA expectations: do they expect our standard hosted SLA or are they asking for an exception (e.g., no autoscale fallback leading to potential throttling)?
3) Variant compatibility: is "redwood-clinical-v1-quant" already validated for their prompt set (tokenization, max seq)? If it requires a custom build, that adds lead time.
4) Can ClinTrial accept a dedicated capacity slot (Reserved) for the pilot? If yes, we can bind the route to that pool and disable cross-region failover.

Operationally, we can implement a route immutability flag that prevents automated fallback, but that increases risk of customer-facing errors during capacity shortfalls. Ops would want:
- Manual failover playbook with approvers (on-call + Eng lead)
- Monitoring/alerting that escalates before request failures (queue depth, cache miss rate)

I'll open OPS ticket OPS-9923 and draft estimated CPU/GPU footprint once I have QPS numbers. Can you ask Dr. Zhao/Paul for expected call volume?

—Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Request: Model route immutability for ClinTrial pilot (EU-bound)

Marissa / team —

Quick legal/leadership notes: committing to an immutable route raises a couple of flags we should not gloss over:

- Indemnity & uptime: if we agree to keep all traffic to a single variant/region and that region becomes degraded, the customer may claim breach of SOW if we do not provide an approved fallback. We should limit contractual guarantees and keep the commitment operational ("we will route to X; in the event of capacity degradation, manual escalation is required").

- Timebox: any exceptional routing binding should be time-limited to the pilot period and subject to periodic review.

- Approvals & delegation: require a signed internal exception (exec + legal + security) that lists the scope and decision owners.

Please loop Contracts to do the SOW redlines — ask Solutions/RevOps to put the proposed language in a tracked SOW. I prefer we avoid hard language that says "no fallback whatsoever"; instead, allow for an "approved manual fallback" process with explicit notification and acceptance terms.

Markus
VP, Product Operations | Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dr. Emily Zhao <e.zhao@clintrial.ai>
Date: Mon, 6 Nov 2028 08:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: Model route immutability for ClinTrial pilot (EU-bound)

Thanks for flagging, Marissa. I reviewed the attached SOC2-summary and the draft asks. Security can provisionally approve an EU-only routing carveout provided the following controls are in place before pilot launch:

1) Customer keys: KMS must be customer-managed for any keys used to encrypt PII-derived artifacts; we need proof-of-possess (IAM policy + key policy) and audit log integration.
2) Audit and retention: enable request-level audit logs for the pilot routes and confirm logs are stored in EU with 30-day retention.
3) Data minimization: strip or tokenise PHI where possible; include a clear list of fields we will not persist.
4) Access controls: isolation of the model serving pool so only the pilot's service accounts can fetch KV caches and models.
5) Runbook: a documented escalation and manual-failover checklist (ops + security sign-off) before we disable automated fallback.

If Karthik is suggesting Reserved capacity, that satisfies isolation requirements better than a shared-hosted carveout. We also need to confirm that telemetry sent to central observability does not include raw prompts — redact at ingest for this pilot.

CC'ing Dr. Zhao so ClinTrial knows the gating items. Once Marissa confirms capacity and the SOW language (timebox + manual fallback), Security can sign off.

—Laura
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Request: Model route immutability for ClinTrial pilot (EU-bound)

Emily / Paul —

Thanks for the prompt review. Internal team has the following consolidated position:

- We can provide an EU-bound, model-bound pilot using a Reserved capacity slot mapped to the variant "redwood-clinical-v1-quant".
- Automatic fallback to non-EU/other variants will be disabled for the pilot window, but manual fallback with explicit approvals (Ops + Eng lead + Security) will be part of the runbook — this is to avoid an SLA exposure where automated fallback could route sensitive data outside EU without a controlled decision.
- Security requires KMS controls, audit logs retained in EU for 30 days, telemetry redaction at ingest, and isolation of the serving pool.
- Legal requests we timebox the immutability to the pilot dates in the SOW and include an approved manual-failover clause.

Next steps / asks for ClinTrial:
1) Please confirm expected peak QPS and avg request size by 2028-11-08 so we can size Reserved capacity.
2) Review the attached route-carveout-spec.xlsx — it lists the operational protections and rollback steps.
3) We'll route a SOW redline from Contracts with the proposed timebox and manual-failover language for signature.

Internal owners: Karthik — create OPS-9923 with capacity estimates once ClinTrial provides QPS. Markus — loop Contracts for the SOW redline. Laura — once we have KMS details and telemetry plan, please issue final sign-off.

I'll schedule a 30-minute sync for 2028-11-09 15:00 CET (invite to follow).

Best,
